items.title: Section: Differentiation Opens — Every Buddha's Realisation Is Identical; Only Their Manifested Forms Differ

items.zh: 一切如來一切功德平等平等無有差別，唯除四法。一者、壽量，二者、名號，三者、族姓，四者、身相。
items.en: Every Tathāgata's every virtue is perfectly, exactly equal, with no difference whatsoever — except for four things: first, lifespan; second, name; third, family lineage; and fourth, bodily appearance.

items.title: The Four Differing Marks Explained — Lifespan, Lineage, and Appearance

items.zh: 一切如來於此四法有增減相，非餘功德。
items.en: Every Tathāgata shows variation only with respect to these four things, never with respect to any other quality.

items.title: Section: A Classical Teaching on Gender and Buddhahood, and Its Own Careful Qualifications

items.zh: 又非女身能證無上正等菩提。何以故？一切菩薩於過第一無數劫時，已捨女身，乃至安坐妙菩提座，曾不為女。
items.en: Moreover, a female form is not one in which unsurpassed, perfect awakening is attained. Why is this? Every bodhisattva, upon passing the first incalculable eon of the path, has already relinquished a female form — and from that point on, including at the very moment of sitting at the seat of awakening itself, is never again female.

items.zh: 一切母邑性多煩惱、性多惡慧。非諸稟性多煩惱身、多惡慧身能證無上正等菩提。
items.en: Every woman, by deeply ingrained habitual tendency, carries more affliction and more distorted views. It is not a body with such deeply ingrained affliction and distorted views that attains unsurpassed, perfect awakening.

items.title: Section: The Chapter on Awakening Closes — and With It, an Entire Structure Spanning Four Fascicles

items.zh: 如是無上正等菩提，如說自性，應如實知；如說最勝，應如實知；如說十種功德名號隨念功德，應如實知；如說出現，應如實知；如說差別，應如實知。
items.en: Unsurpassed, perfect awakening of this kind should be truly known exactly as described regarding its nature; truly known exactly as described regarding its supremacy; truly known exactly as described regarding its ten names for contemplation; truly known exactly as described regarding its manifestation in the world; and truly known exactly as described regarding its differentiation.

items.zh: 又此菩提，為不思議，超過一切尋思道故；為無有量，無邊功德所集成故；為無有上，生成一切聲聞、獨覺及與如來諸功德故；是故唯佛所證菩提，最上、最尊、最妙、最勝。
items.en: This awakening, moreover, is inconceivable, surpassing every path of conceptual thought; immeasurable, composed of boundless virtues; and unsurpassed, giving rise to every virtue possessed by hearers, solitary buddhas, and Tathāgatas alike. For this reason, the awakening realised only by a buddha is the very highest, the most honoured, the most wondrous, and the most supreme.

items.title: Section: "How to Learn" Opens — Seven Points for the Path Ahead

items.zh: 已說菩薩所應學處。如是應學，我今當說。
items.en: Within the Basic Section, the Ground of the Bodhisattva, the first division on yogic practice: the eighth chapter, on the lineage of the powers. What a bodhisattva should learn has already been explained. How this should be learned, I shall now explain.

items.zh: 嗢拕南曰：勝解多、求法、說法、修法行、正教授、教誡、方便攝三業。
items.en: The summarising verse says: abundant resolute conviction, seeking the teaching, teaching it and practising it in accordance with itself, correct instruction and admonishment, and skilful means embracing the three karmas.

items.zh: 若諸菩薩欲於菩薩所應學處精勤修學，最初定應具多勝解，應求正法，應說正法，應正修行法隨法行，應正教授，應正教誡，應住無倒教授、教誡，方便所攝身語意業。云何菩薩具多勝解？

items.title: Section: Abundant Resolute Conviction — Eight Foundations, Beginning With Why the Three Jewels Are Called "Treasures"

items.zh: 謂諸菩薩於其八種勝解依處，具足成就淨信為先決定喜樂。一者、於三寶功德勝解依處，具足成就淨信為先決定喜樂。謂於佛法僧真實功德具多勝解。
items.en: Bodhisattvas, with respect to eight foundations of resolute conviction, accomplish settled joy resting on genuine confidence. ... First, the foundation of conviction in the Three Jewels' virtues: accomplishing settled joy resting on genuine confidence, holding abundant resolute conviction in the genuine virtues of the Buddha, the Dharma, and the Saṅgha.

items.title: Conviction in a Buddha's Power and in True Meaning — Callbacks to Earlier Fascicles

items.zh: 二者、於佛菩薩威力勝解依處，具足成就淨信為先決定喜樂。謂於如前所說威力具多勝解。三者、於真實義勝解依處，具足成就淨信為先決定喜樂。謂於如前所說真實義具多勝解。
items.en: Second, the foundation of conviction in the power of buddhas and bodhisattvas: accomplishing settled joy resting on genuine confidence, holding abundant resolute conviction in the power already described. Third, the foundation of conviction in true meaning: accomplishing settled joy resting on genuine confidence, holding abundant resolute conviction in the true meaning already described.

items.title: Five More Foundations: Cause, Fruit, Attainability, the Means, and the Well-Spoken Teaching

items.zh: 四者、於因勝解依處，具足成就淨信為先決定喜樂。謂於種種如應所攝無顛倒因具多勝解。五者、於果勝解依處，具足成就淨信為先決定喜樂。謂於種種如應所攝無顛倒果具多勝解。六者、於應得義勝解依處，具足成就淨信為先決定喜樂。謂於無上正等菩提所應得義，我有堪任定當能得具多勝解。
items.en: Fourth, the foundation of conviction in cause ... holding abundant resolute conviction in the various genuine, undistorted causes, each sorted as appropriate. Fifth, the foundation of conviction in fruit ... holding abundant resolute conviction in the various genuine, undistorted fruits, each sorted as appropriate. Sixth, the foundation of conviction in what is attainable ... holding abundant resolute conviction that "I possess the capacity, and will certainly attain, the genuine benefit of unsurpassed, perfect awakening."

items.zh: 七者、於得方便勝解依處，具足成就淨信為先決定喜樂。謂於一切菩薩學道能得方便，有此方便得應得義具多勝解。八者、於善言、善語、善說勝解依處，具足成就淨信為先決定喜樂。謂於契經、應頌、記別等法具多勝解。
items.en: Seventh, the foundation of conviction in the means of attainment ... holding abundant resolute conviction in the bodhisattva path's own means of attainment, by which the genuine benefit sought is actually reached. Eighth, the foundation of conviction in good words, good speech, and good teaching ... holding abundant resolute conviction in the discourses, verses, prophetic explanations, and other forms the teaching takes.

items.title: Section: Two Conditions That Cultivate Genuine Conviction, Closing the First of Seven Points

items.zh: 於此八種勝解依處，應知菩薩由二因緣具多勝解。一者、多修勝解故；二者、積集猛利忍故。
items.en: With respect to these eight foundations of resolute conviction, it should be understood that bodhisattvas hold abundant resolute conviction through two conditions: first, through extensively cultivating that very conviction; and second, through accumulating a forceful, unwavering acceptance.

items.title: Section: Seeking the True Teaching — A Bodhisattva Studies Absolutely Everything

items.zh: 彼諸菩薩求正法時，當何所求？云何而求？何義故求？
items.en: When bodhisattvas seek the true teaching, what should they seek? How should they seek it? For what purpose should they seek it?

items.zh: 謂諸菩薩以要言之，當求一切菩薩藏法、聲聞藏法、一切外論、一切世間工業處論。
items.en: Bodhisattvas, in brief, should seek out the entire bodhisattva canon, the hearer canon, every non-Buddhist treatise, and every treatise on worldly crafts and trades.

items.zh: 當知於彼十二分教，方廣一分，唯菩薩藏；所餘諸分，有聲聞藏。一切外論略有三種。一者、因論，二者、聲論，三者、醫方論。一切世間工業處論，非一眾多種種品類。謂金師、鐵師、末尼師等工業智處。

blocks.text: The chapter on awakening closes; the chapter on the lineage of the powers begins. One passage today reflects the gender views of its time; the commentary addresses it directly.
"Every Tathāgata's every virtue is exactly equal, except for four things: lifespan, name, family lineage, and bodily appearance."

The treatise states that awakening is not attained in a female body: "every bodhisattva, upon passing the first incalculable aeon, has already relinquished a female form", and claims women carry "more affliction and distorted views". This reflects the social assumptions of ancient India. The teachers read it as a matter of habit, not essence: Master Cháng Bǎi stresses that ingrained habit is hard to change, and both teachers add that ultimately there is no fixed male or female. It is worth knowing that other Mahāyāna scriptures challenge it sharply: in the *Vimalakīrti Sūtra* a goddess turns Śāriputra into a woman to show that "male" and "female" have no fixed nature, the very point of the chapter on true meaning (Day 318). Readers may weigh the passage in that light.
"Inconceivable, surpassing every path of thought; immeasurable; unsurpassed." Venerable Miào Jìng: we can't reach it by thinking.

The chapter on the lineage of the powers opens with seven points: abundant conviction, seeking the Dharma, teaching it, practising it, instructing, admonishing, and skilful means. Master Cháng Bǎi: "powers" means the ten powers of a Buddha.

Conviction in the Three Jewels' virtues; in the power of Buddhas and bodhisattvas; in true meaning; in cause; in fruit; in the attainability of the goal ("I am capable and will surely attain"; Venerable Miào Jìng: every Buddhist should hold this); in the means; and in the well-spoken teaching.
"The entire bodhisattva canon, the hearer canon, every non-Buddhist treatise, and every treatise on worldly crafts."

quiz.q: "Women by 性 carry more affliction and distorted views." The English reads 性 as habit, not a fixed nature. What do the lectures say?
options: Cháng Bǎi: 性 means hard to change — habit becomes nature; Miào Jìng, after 《披尋記》: the basis is the body, in which affliction and distorted wisdom are established
quiz.why: "Every woman, by deeply ingrained habitual tendency, carries more affliction and more distorted views." Master Cháng Bǎi: 性 carries the sense of being hard to change — habit becomes nature and is then hard to change. Venerable Miào Jìng: "the basis" is the body — affliction and distorted wisdom are established in the body. The English "not a fixed nature" differs from the lectures' emphasis on difficulty of change. (Both masters also say ultimately there are no male or female marks.)

quiz.q: Awakening "is inconceivable, surpassing every path of conceptual thought." What does Venerable Miào Jìng say?
options: thinking can't reach it — it surpasses that domain
quiz.why: "This awakening, moreover, is inconceivable, surpassing every path of conceptual thought." Venerable Miào Jìng: we can't reach it by conceptual thinking — it surpasses that domain.

quiz.q: "The chapter on the lineage of the powers." How does Master Cháng Bǎi explain 力種性?
options: 力 is the ten powers of wisdom; 種 is seed — cause
quiz.why: "Within the Basic Section … the eighth chapter, on the lineage of the powers." Master Cháng Bǎi: 力 means the ten powers, the Buddha's ten powers of wisdom; 種 means seed — cause.

quiz.q: Eight foundations of conviction: "settled joy resting on genuine confidence." How do the masters relate faith and conviction?
options: Miào Jìng: with conviction faith becomes firm — they're one; Cháng Bǎi: earlier faith arose towards persons, here towards the Dharma
quiz.why: "Bodhisattvas, with respect to eight foundations of resolute conviction, accomplish settled joy resting on genuine confidence." Venerable Miào Jìng: after conviction is gained, faith becomes firm — so faith and conviction are one thing. Master Cháng Bǎi: the earlier passage was faith arising towards persons; here, practising on hearing the Dharma's excellence, is faith arising towards the Dharma.

quiz.q: The sixth foundation: conviction that "I am capable and will surely attain." How does Venerable Miào Jìng encourage?
options: every Buddhist should be confident of their own capacity
quiz.why: "Holding abundant resolute conviction that … I am capable and will surely attain." Venerable Miào Jìng: every Buddhist should have this confidence — believing in one's own capacity and ability.

quiz.q: The second condition: "accumulating forceful 忍" — rendered "forbearance." How do the lectures read 忍?
options: Cháng Bǎi: 忍 is the wisdom of acceptance; Miào Jìng: quit at the first discomfort and conviction can't form
quiz.why: "Second, through accumulating a forceful, unwavering forbearance." Master Cháng Bǎi: 忍 is the wisdom of acceptance, by which one has abundant conviction regarding the eight foundations. Venerable Miào Jìng: if at the slightest discomfort you say "I'm not studying, I'm leaving," your conviction can't form. The English "forbearance" takes only the enduring sense.

quiz.q: Bodhisattvas should seek "every non-Buddhist treatise and every treatise on crafts." What does Master Cháng Bǎi say?
options: every worldly domain — medicine, science, literature, even the kitchen
quiz.why: "Bodhisattvas, in brief, should seek out the entire bodhisattva canon, the hearer canon, every non-Buddhist treatise, and every treatise on worldly crafts and trades." Master Cháng Bǎi: every worldly domain — medicine, science, literature, even kitchen matters.
